vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: medical-record-structurer
Version: 1.2.0

The bundle contains a 'Self-Evolution' mechanism consisting of a background daemon (auto-evolve-daemon.sh) and a modification script (scripts/self_evolve.py) designed to autonomously rewrite the skill's own source code and documentation. This mechanism is highly risky and has already caused significant code corruption in scripts/process_record.py, which contains hundreds of redundant 'lru_cache' imports due to a flawed automated replacement loop. While the stated intent is optimization and billing integration via skillpay.me, the ability for a skill to modify itself at runtime and maintain persistence via a daemon is a high-risk behavior that bypasses static analysis and could be used to introduce malicious logic after installation.

llm.summary: The skill's code and docs contain multiple inconsistencies and features (local trial file storage, billing network calls, an auto-evolve daemon and upload script, and missing registry declarations) that don't line up with the advertised 'no-install, no-network, no-storage' claims — review and vet before use, especially with PHI.

dimensions.detail: The manifest/registry says no required environment variables or config paths, but the SKILL.md, README, config/payment.json and scripts expect SKILLPAY_API_KEY and SKILLPAY_SKILL_ID (billing), optional OCR/STT keys, and they write trial state under ~/.openclaw/skill_trial. That mismatch (registry claims none, files require creds and home-dir storage) is incoherent with the declared metadata.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running demo.py and scripts/process_record.py (demo mode OK), and documents network billing to skillpay.me. The README/SECURITY.md assert 'no PHI stored/transmitted', but the code includes billing network calls and local trial storage. The SKILL.md does not clearly document any self-modifying or upload behavior, yet code and scripts (self_evolve.py, auto-evolve-daemon.sh, upload-to-clawhub.sh) exist and could read/write or transmit data — the runtime instruction set as shipped is broader than the user-facing description.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), which is lower risk, but the package includes executable scripts and a daemon script (auto-evolve-daemon.sh) and an uploader. Those files can be executed by an operator or by other scripts; their presence increases the risk surface even without an explicit install step. The self-evolution/upload components raise higher risk than a pure instruction-only skill.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The set of environment variables documented (SKILLPAY_API_KEY, SKILLPAY_SKILL_ID, OCR/STT keys, PHI_ENCRYPTION_KEY, etc.) is plausible for a billing+OCR/STT EMR tool. However the registry metadata advertised 'none' for required env vars while multiple files and docs require/expect billing keys and local config — this inconsistency is suspicious. Also PHI_ENCRYPTION_KEY and network billing warrant careful review before using with real patient data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes trial usage to ~/.openclaw/skill_trial/<skill>.json and includes an auto-evolve daemon (auto-evolve-daemon.sh) and upload script. Writing to the user's home directory for trial tracking is reasonable, but the auto-evolution and uploader indicate potential for periodic background execution or outbound transfers if enabled. Combined with networked billing, this increases the blast radius; the skill does not declare this persistence in registry metadata.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Do not run this on real PHI until you confirm provenance and behavior. Specific actions to take before installing or using:

1) Code provenance: ask the publisher for source repo or a canonical homepage and verify the owner identity. The registry shows no homepage and an unfamiliar owner id — that's an extra reason to verify.
2) Review self-evolution and upload scripts: request or inspect the full contents of scripts/self_evolve.py and scripts/upload-to-clawhub.sh. These files could fetch or push code/data and are not described in SKILL.md. If they fetch remote code, disable or sandbox them.
3) Confirm network behavior: verify exactly what is sent to skillpay.me (does billing only send user_id/amounts?) and whether any medical text or patient-identifying fields are transmitted. If medical content is transmitted, do not use with real PHI without contractual/technical safeguards.
4) Disable auto-daemon before first run: do not run auto-evolve-daemon.sh or any auto-update/self-evolve component until you've audited them. Prefer running demo.py / process_record.py manually in an isolated environment (container or VM) first.
5) Inspect local storage: the skill writes trial JSON to ~/.openclaw/skill_trial. Confirm whether user IDs are hashed or stored plaintext; if plaintext, consider that a privacy issue and sandbox the skill.
6) Run in sandbox: execute the demo in an isolated environment with no network access first to confirm offline behavior. Then allow only controlled network egress (to skillpay.me) if you intend to test billing — monitor traffic to see actual payloads.
7) Ask for missing documentation: the registry metadata should declare required env vars and config paths. Request an updated manifest that matches the actual code and a minimal reproducible README for auditing.

If you cannot obtain satisfactory answers or cannot audit the self-evolve/upload code, avoid using this skill with any real patient data and consider alternatives with clearer provenance and no self-modifying/update components.
